significance.protein: Marker of glomerular or tubular injury. Persistent proteinuria is associated with CKD progression and cardiovascular risk (quantitative albuminuria recommended).
significance.glucose: Appears when blood glucose exceeds the renal threshold (~180 mg/dL). Suggests possible diabetes or poor glycemic control (check fasting glucose and HbA1c).
significance.blood: Hematuria — requires differentiation among urolithiasis, infection, glomerulonephritis and tumor. If persistent, consider imaging and urine cytology.
significance.leukocyte: Pyuria — suggests urinary tract infection. Interpret together with nitrite and symptoms.
significance.nitrite: Suggests gram-negative (enteric) bacterial infection. Combined with leukocytes, the likelihood of UTI increases.
significance.ketone: Ketonuria — diabetic ketoacidosis, starvation or low-carbohydrate diet. Take care when accompanied by hyperglycemia.
significance.bilirubin: A clue to hepatobiliary disease (obstructive jaundice, hepatocellular injury). Link with liver function tests.
significance.urobilinogen: When elevated, hemolysis or hepatocellular disease is possible. Interpret together with bilirubin.
significance.specific_gravity: Reflects renal concentrating ability and hydration status. A clue to dehydration or diabetes insipidus.
significance.ph: A clue to acid-base status, stone type and urinary tract infection. Persistent alkaline urine suggests urease-producing bacterial infection.
significance.vitamin_c: Assay interferent — at high concentrations it can cause false negatives for occult blood and urine glucose. Take care when interpreting results.

kidney.reference: KDIGO 2024 CKD guideline — risk stratification based on eGFR and albuminuria/ACR (green/yellow/orange/red)
kidney.staging: Semi-quantitative urine protein is a screening step. Confirmation and staging require serum creatinine (eGFR) and quantitative ACR.
kidney.followup: Suggested: serum creatinine and eGFR, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (uACR), nephrology referral if needed.

diabetes.reference: Korean Diabetes Association / ADA — fasting glucose and HbA1c diagnostic criteria (urine glucose is a supporting indicator)
diabetes.staging: Positive urine glucose suggests possible hyperglycemia but is not a diagnostic criterion. Confirm with fasting glucose and HbA1c.
diabetes.followup: Suggested: fasting glucose and HbA1c, screening for diabetic complications (renal, retinal).

hypertension.reference: Korean Society of Hypertension — office and home blood pressure classification, target organ damage assessment
hypertension.staging: Proteinuria is used as an indicator of hypertensive target organ (kidney) damage. Interpret together with blood pressure readings.
hypertension.followup: Suggested: repeated blood pressure measurement, urine albumin, and risk factor assessment such as ECG and lipids.

uti.reference: UTI practice guideline — pyuria, nitrite and symptoms combined, differentiating asymptomatic bacteriuria
uti.staging: Positive leukocytes and nitrite with voiding symptoms suggest UTI. Asymptomatic cases may not require treatment.
uti.followup: Suggested: urine culture and antibiotic susceptibility when symptomatic; evaluate the cause in recurrent cases.

liver.reference: Hepatobiliary assessment — bilirubin and urobilinogen pattern plus liver function tests
liver.staging: Urine bilirubin and urobilinogen are supporting clues. The pattern (obstructive vs. hepatocellular) needs to be differentiated.
liver.followup: Suggested: liver function tests (AST/ALT/ALP/total bilirubin), imaging if needed.
